naive_baseline.description: Original sort-merge direct apply: unbucketed, serial, single-thread; the initial engine design (Phase 6)
naive_baseline.commit_short_desc: Phase 6: sort-merge engine + propagate with Direction
known_confounders: Lacks parallel implementation
No bucketing (uses lex sort on all terms per layer)
No channel prepare optimization
No truncation or TopN support in initial version
naive_baseline.notes: This commit introduced the initial sort-merge pipeline. The algorithm is unbucketed and serial, making it a natural baseline for comparing against later bucketing and parallelization improvements.

direct_small_sum_path.description: Direct-apply hash-map path for small sums (< 2048 terms by default); bypasses bucketing and prepare for low-m regimes
direct_small_sum_path.commit_short_desc: feat: add a runtime-selectable direct-apply small-sum path
known_confounders: Orthogonal to bucketed path; only activated for small sums (< threshold)
Does not apply per-layer finalization for truncation policies
No bucketing, no coset span, no sort
direct_small_sum_path.notes: Introduced as an opt-in EngineSelection::Auto path. Not the focus for mid-range benchmarks (1e5-1e6 terms) but valuable for showing the per-layer fixed-cost landscape. Verified in FINDINGS.md as 2.28-2.36x faster on small-m kicked-Ising.

bucketed_engine_serial.description: Bucketed sort-merge engine, single-threaded version (v0.2 B.5): introduces GF(2)-linear hash bucketing and bucket-local sorting
bucketed_engine_serial.commit_short_desc: v0.2 B.5: the bucketed layer engine, sequential
known_confounders: Serial execution (no parallelization yet)
Removes the global sort; replaces with bucket-local sorts
Introduces GF(2)-linear hash for bucketing
Includes channel prepare optimization
bucketed_engine_serial.notes: This is the core bucketing innovation. Measured ~15x speedup on depolarizing layer at 1e6 terms when parallelized in v0.2 C.1. Single-thread performance vs d410f4e shows the algorithmic win of bucketing alone.

bucketed_engine_parallel.description: Bucketed engine with Rayon parallelization (v0.2 C.1-C.3): adds thread-level parallelism via write-disjoint bucket cosets
bucketed_engine_parallel.commit_short_desc: v0.2 C.1-C.3: parallelize the engine, then fix what measurement exposed
known_confounders: Introduces parallel bucket loop via rayon::par_iter_mut
Also refactors rescale_in_place to parallel
Includes improved truncation finalization and benchmarking suite
Adds byte-identity tests across thread counts
bucketed_engine_parallel.notes: Reported 60.3ms -> 1.12ms on Depolarizing (54x), 7.93x thread scaling on rotation at 32 threads. The write-disjoint bucket cosets enable lock-free parallelism. This is the canonical bucketed engine as shipped.

presentation_bench_crate_variants.description: Presentation benchmark crate with four isolated implementations for comparison: naive (direct loop), per-thread-map (work-stealing maps), mergesort (parallel mergesort), and bucketed (reference impl)
presentation_bench_crate_variants.commit_short_desc: presentation: bench crate — naive, per-thread-map, mergesort and bucketed variants with agreement tests
known_confounders: Independent implementations in the bench crate, not the core library
Includes agreement tests to verify all four produce identical results
Single workload fixture shared across all variants
Simplified interfaces compared to full engine (no truncation, no channels)
presentation_bench_crate_variants.notes: Checkout commit 81b922c and run `cargo run --release -p presentation-bench`. Provides apples-to-apples A/B between threadmaps (rejected), mergesort (attempted), and bucketed (shipped). Also available at later commits (2b2caca) with updated lockfile.

partitioned_numa_engine.description: Partitioned engine with in-process NUMA domains (PR #6): splits sum across P ≤ 16 NUMA domains via GF(2)-partition rows, one pinned Rayon pool per partition, write-disjoint by construction
known_confounders: Bundles in-process NUMA partitioning, MPI support, and exchange protocol
Introduces PartitionRows::cut policy for selecting partition boundaries
Includes new phase-timing instrumentation and exchange optimization
Adds distributed sum support (MpiTransport) alongside in-process
Incompatible with exact TopN (ApproxTopN substituted at compile time)
partitioned_numa_engine.notes: Measured -4.1% to -18.2% on dense layers at P=2; 2-8x cost multiplier on layers with remote deltas. Set P=1 for single-process reference (byte-identical to bucketed engine). Use `--partitions 2 --partition-cpus '<cpu_list>'` on phase_breakdown probe.

jcc_erratum_and_branch_prediction.description: Front-end campaign: JCC branch padding (SKX102 erratum fix), branch-prediction optimization (merge split + branchless gather filter), and radix gate second arm
jcc_erratum_and_branch_prediction.commit_short_desc: Front-end campaign: JCC erratum, branch prediction, and the radix gate — −23..−28% on sparse layers (#7)
known_confounders: JCC padding flag (scripts/jcc-rustflags.sh) is CPU-dependent; not in base .cargo/config
Bundles three distinct optimizations: padding (DSB fix), merge split (branch prediction), radix gate arm
Radix gate second arm adds conditional logic for rest_streams >= 3 && rest_rows_per_key < 2
The padding is a ~1% tax on non-affected systems; included via detection script
XOR-fold popcount reduction is null on latency-bound layers but bitwise identical
jcc_erratum_and_branch_prediction.notes: Reported -23% to -28% on sparse layers (su4, rotation_zz); -14.68% on rotation_zz from branch prediction alone (40% of misses removed). JCC padding brings DSB residency from 45.8% to 97.9%. Measurement must source jcc-rustflags.sh to apply padding on affected systems.

attempted_rejected_variants.description: Attempted but rejected approaches recorded in research/FINDINGS.md: per-thread-maps (1.25-1.9x slower), parallel mergesort (overtaken by bucketing), SIMD kernels (layout cost > ISA gain), static coset placement (stragglers cost locality), branchless merge (cmov adds dependency)
attempted_rejected_variants.commit_short_desc: See research/FINDINGS.md for full protocols and raw A/B tables
known_confounders: These are reported measurements, not current code
Full reproduction protocols in deleted research/notes/ (git show branch:research/notes/YYYY-MM-DD-*.md)
Some (e.g., static coset placement) are inherently architecture-dependent
attempted_rejected_variants.notes: Not suitable for live benchmarking. Instead, read FINDINGS.md sections: 'Static coset→worker placement' (1.25-1.9x slower), 'Segment-copy merge' (+36.3% on cnot), 'Interleaved transient key layout' (+1.9% on gu2q), 'Branchless merge2_into' (+4.83% on rotation_zz).
